reason: The cited evidence supports that semi-coherent boundaries resist dislocation penetration and that pile-ups can lead to cracking, but it provides no support for the key premises that aging will nucleate coherent precipitates at interfaces, that such precipitates will reduce pile-ups, or that this will improve ductility while maintaining strength.
premises: Semi-coherent phase boundaries in the eutectic HEA are strong and resist dislocation penetration, reducing pile-ups in the BCC phase.
Dislocation pile-ups at these boundaries can facilitate crack nucleation.
Coherent nanoprecipitates can be selectively nucleated at lamellar colony interfaces by aging.
Coherent precipitates at interfaces will reduce dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentrations.
Reducing pile-ups will enhance ductility while retaining or increasing strength.
